earlier_scan.source_named: No grammar or phonology of Shama-Sambuga located; only Kainji comparative wordlist material referenced

sources.citation: OLAC inventory for the Kamuku cluster [cdr] (the Internet Archive 2025) and Blench 2011 'Kamuku languages' web page (rogerblench.info, the Internet Archive 2015)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only 'language description' item for any Kamuku lect is Mort 2012 (Cinda phonology, SIL 93650, not online) -- for Cinda [cdr], not Shama. Blench's Kamuku page is a classification blurb; the the Internet Archive's index shows no wordlist/phonology PDF was ever posted in that folder.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Paywalled shell: classification and alternate names Tushama, Ushama only; no typology field.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Stuart McGill. 2012. The Kainji languages of northwestern and central Nigeria. Circulation draft, May 2012. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 369 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 3.5.5 'Shama-Sambuga' (p.16) is sociolinguistic only ('quite divergent lexically'); sec. 4.5.3 'Shama' (p.34), the slot for a phonology, is an EMPTY heading. Stress/accent do not occur anywhere in the 369-pp draft; Shama forms in the comparative tables carry no tone marks.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page sham1278 (refs: Blench n.d., McGill 2009, McGill 2012 subclassification; Dettweiler & Dettweiler 2003; Yoder et al. 2014)
sources.note: No grammar, phonology or sketch listed for the language; Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology.

sources.citation: PARADISEC RB5-Kainji_Kamuku_wordlists (Yoder, Zachariah, compiler, 2007), OAI-PMH record
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Audio of the 2007 survey wordlists; languages given: Cinda, Igwama, Kagare, Kuki, Kuru, Regi -- no Shama recording.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 4th ed. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. Entry 412 'Shama-Sambuga cluster'
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lists only 'Source(s) Blench (1987); Regnier (1992)' (unpublished wordlists); Shama at Ushama [=Kawo], 15 km NW of Kagara; Sambuga 'Possibly extinct (2008)'. No phonology reference.

sources.citation: Yoder, Zachariah, Katarína Hannelová, Carol Magnusson, Yakubu Oro, Linus Otronyi, Michael J. Rueck & Katharine Spencer. 2014. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the 'Yara (Kamuku) people, Niger and Kaduna States, Nigeria. Jos: Language Development Facilitators. vi+77 pp. (SIL archive entry 60335)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey; Shama [sqa] treated in secs 1.3, 3.2, 3.4.5, 6.6 (vital, village Kawo; Sambuga extinct, no speaker found); a >100-word Shama wordlist (Kawo, Nov 2007) used only for lexicostatistics (Table 3-5: 59-70% with 'Yara). The words stress/accent/tone do not occur in the report.

sources.citation: McGill, Stuart & Roger Blench. 2012. Documentation, development, and ideology in the northwestern Kainji languages. Language Documentation and Description 11: 90-135
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Documentation-status table (p.100): 'Tushama -- Unpublished wordlists (Dettweiler & Dettweiler 2002, KJ700)'; 'Tusambuga (dagger)'. Confirms no phonological description of Shama exists.

sources.citation: Magnusson, Carol, Zach Yoder & Linus Otronyi (transcribers). 2007. Wordlist: Kamuku [cdr] Kagare and Shama dialects [Kagare: Ungwan Tanko; Shama: Kawo]. SIL Nigeria Group Word List field sheets, 18 pp. SIL archive entry 82877
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Handwritten scanned elicitation sheets (no text layer; 200-dpi scanned of pp.1-2 unusable); no tone or stress marking visible, no statement.

sources.citation: Dettweiler, Stephen H. & Sonia G. Dettweiler. 2003 [ms 1993/2002]. Sociolinguistic survey (level one) of the Kamuku language cluster. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2003-003. 37 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p.6: 'Although Kamuku and Acipa are known to be tone languages, our word lists do not attempt to show tone'. Contains a Shama wordlist (Kagara, Revd Mu'azu Bahago, 14 Mar 1992, elicited by Clark D. Regnier) in Appendix A, untoned; Shama 64% lexically similar to Cinda, a 'small, isolated' subgroup.

sources.citation: Mort, Katharine. 2012. A Phonological Description of the Cinda [tʃìndɨ́] dialect of the Kamuku language. Draft ms., 66 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 93650 (has ch. 8 Tone, ch. 9 Stress)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Not Shama (Cinda-Regi-Tiyal, cind1241/cdr), but the only phonology of any Kamuku lect and the only one with a stress chapter; would give the nearest-relative template for what a Shama description might say

sources.citation: Yoder, Zachariah et al. 2007. Kamuku survey wordlists and audio (SIL archive entries 82784-82883; PARADISEC RB5-Kainji_Kamuku_wordlists) -- Shama entry 82877 downloaded; any Shama audio not located
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: If a Shama audio recording exists anywhere it would allow an instrumental look at prominence; PARADISEC record lists no Shama audio

sources.citation: Regnier, Clark D. 1992. Kamuku wordlists (incl. Shama, Kagara, 14 Mar 1992; the 'Regnier (1992)' of Blench's Atlas). Unpublished SIL Nigeria ms; the Shama list is printed untoned in Dettweiler & Dettweiler 2003, Appendix A
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only primary data on Shama cited by Blench (2019) and McGill & Blench (2012); if an original with tone/stress marking exists it would be the closest thing to a description

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 1987/1988. [Kamuku / Basa-Kamuku fieldnotes and wordlists incl. Shama and Sambuga; 'The internal structure of the Basa-Kamuku languages', paper 1988]; and the KJ700 comparative Kainji wordlist database
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: First report of Shama and Sambuga (Blench & McGill 2012, sec. 3.5.5); the Sambuga data may be the only record of that now-extinct lect; Blench's own site is captcha/squatted and the Kamuku folder never held these files
